content.title: About
content.content: Ravioli are small pasta parcels stuffed with a seasoned ground‑meat filling (usually beef, pork, or a blend). They are served hot, drenched in a smooth cream sauce that enhances the savory filling.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Ravioli originated in Italy, where each region has its own traditional shapes and fillings.
Meat fillings are often flavored with herbs such as basil, oregano, and parsley.
The cream sauce is typically made from heavy cream, butter, and a touch of Parmesan cheese.
Ravioli can be homemade or industrially produced; factory‑made pasta often contains extra egg for elasticity.
In Italy, ravioli are commonly served as a primo (first course) during family meals.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: The meat filling provides complete, high‑quality protein essential for muscle repair and growth.

items.title: Source of iron
items.content: Beef and pork contain heme iron, which is readily absorbed by the body.

items.title: Contains vitamin B12
items.content: Vitamin B12 supports nervous system function and red blood cell formation.

items.title: Calcium from the cream sauce
items.content: Cream and cheese add calcium, contributing to bone health.

items.title: Sustained energy
items.content: The combination of carbohydrates from the pasta and fats in the sauce provides lasting satiety.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: The dish is rich in fats and carbs, so portion control is advisable for weight‑management diets.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Wheat‑based pasta contains gluten, which can trigger reactions in people with celiac disease.

items.title: Saturated fat
items.content: The cream sauce adds saturated fat, which may affect cholesterol levels if consumed excessively.

items.title: Sodium
items.content: Cream sauces are often salted; individuals with hypertension should limit intake.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the ravioli hot, spooned with the cream sauce. Garnish with fresh herbs, grated Parmesan, or toasted pine nuts. Pairs well with a light white wine or a dry rosé.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cooked ravioli refrigerated in an airtight container for 2‑3 days, storing the sauce separately. Freeze in sealed bags at –18 °C for longer storage; thaw in the fridge before reheating.
